transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my daughter insisted I come in. She drove me here in her new Honda... she used to have a Ford, but the transmission gave out right before Thanksgiving. Turkeys were so expensive this year anyway. I see the prices every day at work—I've been a cashier on register four for years. They just moved the whole candy aisle last week, and people get so upset when they can't find the peppermints. 

But... she brought me here because I keep telling them I’m the reason my friend died. I just... I didn’t call her back when I was supposed to. And I had ugly thoughts sometimes. Just awful, ugly thoughts. It’s why things are going wrong everywhere. Even at church, I know the Lord is punishing everybody there because of me. The roof leaked right over the choir last Sunday, and I just sat in the pew knowing it was all my fault.
Can you tell me more about these ugly thoughts and why you think they're connected to your friend's death and other things going wrong?

Well, the ugly thoughts... they were just so mean. I'd think about how she never remembered my birthday, and I'd get mad. And then I didn't call her back that Tuesday. Or maybe it was Wednesday. It rained all day Wednesday, I remember because my shoes got soaked waiting for the bus. The 42 bus is always late when it rains, and the driver, Frank—he retired last month, actually—he always used to say the wipers were broken. 

But I know it's my fault she's gone, and now everything else is ruined too. It's like I have this rot inside me. When I'm at church now... it's so clear. When the pastor says the prayers, or when the choir sings certain lines, I know they aren't just singing. They're looking right at me. They're warning me that God has marked me. I brought all this suffering on us, on the whole congregation. The roof leaking, the organ breaking down last Easter... my sister used to play the organ, you know. She had arthritis so bad in her hands, she had to stop. She tried those copper bracelets, but I don't think they do a lick of good. But yes, God marked me because of what I did, and the pastor knows it. Everyone knows it.
Do you really believe that your thoughts or actions could cause external events like the church roof leaking?

Oh, I don't just believe it, Doctor. I know it. It's as plain as the nose on your face. When Pastor Miller says the morning prayers, or... or when the choir sings certain lines from the hymnal, I know they are really warning me. They're looking right at me because they know God has marked me. 

The choir robes are this awful maroon color now, by the way. They used to be a lovely royal blue, but Mrs. Higgins—she's the head of the hospitality committee—she insisted on maroon to match the new carpeting in the vestibule. I always thought the blue was much nicer. It really brought out my daughter's eyes when she used to sing alto with them. She stopped singing when she started nursing school, though. Nursing school is just so expensive these days. I see the young students at my register buying nothing but instant noodles and cheap white bread. It just breaks your heart how much a loaf of bread costs now. We had to raise the price on the store brand twice since October. 

But... oh, what was I saying? The church, yes. The church is suffering because I brought this on us. God marked me for my ugly thoughts, and now the whole congregation has to pay for my sins with the roof and everything else. The roofer they hired to fix that leak, Mr. Abernathy... he actually comes through my line on Tuesdays. He always buys two packs of chewing tobacco and a Diet Coke. I tell him it's going to rot his teeth right out of his head, but he just laughs at me. He doesn't understand what real rot feels like.
How do you feel about yourself when you think about not calling your friend back?

I just feel... I feel like garbage. Less than garbage. I'm a terrible, wicked person. I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly, hateful thoughts about her, and now she's dead. It's my fault. I keep telling my daughter that, but she doesn't want to hear it. She just turns up the radio in that Honda of hers. It has satellite radio, you know. Hundreds of stations. I don't know why anyone needs that many stations. In my day, we had AM and FM, and we were perfectly happy listening to the local news and the weather report. The weatherman on Channel 4, he always wears those loud plaid suits. I don't know who tells him those look good. 

But I deserve to feel this way. I'm worthless. I'm the reason she died, and I'm the reason the Lord is punishing everybody at church. I brought this rot on all of them. The roof, the organ... it's all because I'm so awful inside. I shouldn't even be allowed around decent people.
Do you feel guilty about anything else besides not calling your friend back and having those ugly thoughts about her?

Anything else? I... well, isn't that enough to ruin everything? I just keep telling them... I tell my daughter, and I even tried to tell Kevin at work. Kevin is the shift manager at the grocery store. He’s only twenty-two, barely older than my grandson, and he’s always rearranging the produce section. He puts the Honeycrisp apples right at the front now. They’re nearly three dollars a pound! Who on earth can afford three dollars a pound for apples? I remember when you could get a whole sack for that. My mother used to make apple butter in this big copper kettle out in the yard... it took all day, just stirring and stirring with a long wooden paddle. 

But I told Kevin, I keep telling them all, I’m the reason my friend died. Just because I didn’t call her back and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. And it doesn't stop with her. I know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. The whole congregation is suffering for what I am. I tried to tell Pastor Miller that, too, but he just patted my hand. He has very soft hands for a man. Not like my husband’s hands. My husband was a mechanic, you know. The black grease used to get right down into his fingerprints, and you could never scrub it out, no matter how much of that gritty orange soap we bought at the hardware store...
Do you think you would still feel responsible for your friend's death if everyone around you, including your family and Pastor Miller, told you it wasn't your fault?

They already tell me that, Doctor. My daughter says it, and Pastor Miller... well, he tries to be kind about it. But their words don't change what I know in my bones. Like I was trying to tell you before, I hear it every single Sunday. When the pastor says the morning prayers, or when the choir sings certain lines, I know they are really warning me. They know God has marked me, and they know the church is suffering because I brought this on us. 

The choir... they sing from those old red Cokesbury hymnals, you know. We've had them since 1982, I think. The pages are all yellowed now and the bindings are just falling to pieces. I tried to fix a few of them last month with some clear packing tape, but you know how that tape gets over time... it turns all yellow and sticky on the edges and picks up every little piece of lint. My daughter uses that exact same tape when she mails Christmas presents to her cousin in Ohio. Ohio gets just terribly cold in the winter. I remember taking a Greyhound bus through Cleveland once in January, back in the seventies, and the heater on the bus was broken the entire trip. We all had to sit there shivering in our heavy winter coats. I had this lovely wool coat with a faux fur collar back then, but I accidentally left it at a diner in Toledo... they had the best cherry pie at that diner, though. Real tart cherries, not that syrupy canned filling you get at the store nowadays.
Do you feel guilty about things that happened before your friend passed away?

Before she passed? No... no, I didn't feel this way before. I mean, before she died and I sank down into this awful, heavy feeling, I never believed the choir or Pastor Miller were sending warnings about me. None of that. Those thoughts only started after I became so low and guilty these past few weeks. It just hit me all at once, you know? Like a sudden storm rolling in off the plains. 

We used to get the most terrible thunderstorms when I was a little girl growing up. The sky would turn this bruised, greenish-purple color, and my mother would make us all go down into the root cellar. It smelled like damp earth and old potatoes down there. We kept all the canned goods on these rickety wooden shelves my grandfather built. He used pine, I think. Or maybe it was cedar? Cedar smells so nice, doesn't it? I bought a cedar block for my closet just last month to keep the moths away from my winter sweaters. Moths will just ruin a good wool sweater before you even know they're in there. I had a beautiful cardigan, powder blue with pearl buttons, and I went to put it on for church one Sunday and there was a hole right in the sleeve, big as a quarter. You can't mend a hole that big without it looking like a terrible scar, no matter how careful you are with the needle. My eyesight isn't what it used to be for sewing anyway. I had to get bifocals two years ago. The frames are sort of a tortoiseshell pattern. They were very expensive, even with the discount at the eye doctor...
Do you feel guilty about things that have nothing to do with your friend's death or the church?

No, no, it's just... it's just her, and the church. Like I keep telling them, I'm the reason she died, because I didn't call her back and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. And now the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. It's a terrible burden to carry, knowing you've ruined everything for everyone. I mean, the church has been there since... well, since before I was born. 

They built the original sanctuary in 1912, I think. Or maybe 1914? It has those beautiful stained glass windows. The one on the east side has a picture of the Good Shepherd, and the morning light comes through it just so. The glass is all ruby red and cobalt blue. You don't see colors like that anymore. My grandmother had a cobalt blue glass vase that she kept on her dining room table. She used to put fresh lilacs in it every spring. The smell of lilacs is just heavenly, isn't it? We had a huge lilac bush in our backyard when I was growing up, right next to the clothesline. My mother would hang the sheets out to dry, and they'd blow in the wind and catch the scent of the flowers. There's nothing quite like sleeping on sheets that have dried in the fresh air. Nowadays people just toss everything in the dryer with those little scented sheets, but it's not the same. The dryer makes everything so staticky, too. I pulled a sweater out of the dryer the other day and it crackled like a bowl of Rice Krispies. I used to love Rice Krispies when I was a girl, especially if you put a spoonful of sugar on top...
Do you feel guilty about your relationship with your family members, aside from your daughter?

No, it's really just what I was saying before. My family... they're fine. It's just my friend, and the church. Like I keep telling them, I'm the reason she died. Because I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. And now I just know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. It's all my fault. 

I used to call her every Tuesday evening, right after Jeopardy. We both loved Jeopardy. Alex Trebek was such a wonderful host, wasn't he? Always so dignified. He wore such nice suits. My husband, God rest his soul, he had a lovely charcoal gray suit he wore to our daughter's wedding. We bought it at a little men's shop downtown that closed years ago. It was right next to a bakery that sold the most wonderful eclairs. They had real custard inside, not that pudding stuff they use now. The baker was a nice Italian man, Mr. Rossi. He always gave my daughter a free cookie when we went in. She loved those little butter cookies with the sprinkles on top. Sprinkles always get everywhere, though. I found one under the refrigerator just last week when I was sweeping. I try to sweep every day, but this old broom I have is losing its bristles. I really need to go to the hardware store and get a new one, but the parking lot there is always so crowded...
Do you ever have days where you don't feel guilty about not calling your friend back?

No, there's never a day without it. I just... I keep telling everyone, I'm the reason she died. If I had just picked up the phone, if I hadn't had those ugly thoughts about her sometimes... it's all my fault. And now the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me. I just know it. It's a terrible thing, knowing you've brought ruin on a place so holy. 

Our church has the most beautiful organ, you know. It's a pipe organ, installed back in the fifties. The pipes go all the way up to the ceiling, all shiny and brass. The organist, Mrs. Higgins, she's been playing it since I was a young woman. She must be nearly ninety now, but her hands just fly over those keys. She always wore these lovely lace gloves, even in the summer. I tried wearing gloves like that once to a garden party, but they made my hands sweat terribly. It was one of those humid August afternoons where the air just hangs on you like a wet blanket. We served iced tea with fresh mint from my garden. Mint grows like a weed if you aren't careful. It completely took over my tomato patch one year. I had the most beautiful beefsteak tomatoes, big as softballs. There's nothing better than a fresh tomato sandwich with a little mayonnaise and salt on white bread. You have to use the soft white bread, the kind that sticks to the roof of your mouth a little bit. My daughter used to hate the crusts, so I'd cut them off and feed them to the birds. The blue jays were always the first to come down for them...
Do you feel guilty about things that have nothing to do with your friend or the church?

No, doctor, I... I thought I just said that. It's really just my friend, and the church. Like I keep telling them, I'm the reason she died. Because I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. And now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. It's just awful, knowing you've caused so much suffering. 

My friend, she used to suffer from terrible arthritis in her knees. Some days she could barely walk up the steps to the church. They really ought to put a ramp in, you know. I mentioned it to Pastor Thomas once, but he said the historical society wouldn't allow them to alter the front steps. They're made of this beautiful gray stone, granite I think. Granite is so durable, isn't it? My cousin in Ohio put granite countertops in her kitchen when she remodeled. It cost a small fortune, but it looked just gorgeous. She had these cherry wood cabinets that matched perfectly. Cherry wood gets darker as it ages, you know. It's funny how things change color over time. Like my hair... I used to have the thickest auburn hair when I was a girl. Now it's just thin and white. I buy this special shampoo at the drugstore that's supposed to make it look fuller, but it smells a bit like medicine. The drugstore on Main Street used to have a soda fountain in the back when I was little. You could get a cherry phosphate for a nickel. A nickel doesn't buy anything these days, does it? I found a shiny 1964 nickel in my change purse yesterday when I was at the grocery store. I always check the dates on coins...
Do you think there's any possibility that your belief about being the reason for your friend's death might not be true?

No, there's no possibility it isn't true. I know it for a fact. Because... well, when the pastor says the prayers on Sunday morning, or when the choir sings certain lines, I know they are really warning me. They're sending me a message that God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. I can hear it in the way they sing. 

The choir has such lovely voices, though, especially the sopranos. They stand in the back row, right under the big stained glass window with the doves on it. That window was donated by the Miller family after the terrible storm in '85. It hailed so hard that day, the hailstones were the size of golf balls. They completely dented the roof of my husband's Buick. It was a LeSabre, light blue with a white vinyl top. You really don't see cars with vinyl tops anymore, do you? They used to get so hot in the summer sun, if you touched the roof it would burn your hand right through your gardening gloves. I always wore gloves when I pulled weeds, because of the thistles. Thistles have those awful little purple flowers that look pretty but prick you if you aren't careful. I tried to grow petunias in that spot instead, but the soil was too acidic. You have to add lime to the soil if it's too acidic. You can buy it in big heavy bags at the garden center, but I can't lift those bags anymore. My back just isn't what it used to be since I started working the register at the grocery store. Standing on that hard linoleum floor all day really takes it out of your knees...
Do you ever have moments where you don't feel guilty about your friend's death?

I feel like a broken record, doctor, but no, there isn't a single moment. I keep telling everyone the same thing because it's the truth... I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts about her sometimes. It's a terrible burden, knowing the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. I really should have just picked up the phone. 

We used to talk on the phone for hours. I still have one of those old rotary phones in my kitchen, actually. It's harvest gold, mounted right on the wall by the pantry. The cord on it is so long, I could stretch it all the way across the kitchen to the stove while I was cooking. I used to make a pot roast every Sunday. You have to sear the meat first to lock in the juices, my mother taught me that. She was a wonderful cook, but she never measured a single ingredient. Just a pinch of this and a dash of that. I tried to bake her famous pound cake for the church bake sale a few years back, but it fell completely flat in the middle. It was just so embarrassing. I had to run to the grocery store and buy a store-made one before my shift started. Working the register, I see people buying those bakery cakes all the time. They always buy the ones with the whipped icing, but I think buttercream holds up much better if it's sitting out. Especially for birthday parties. My grandson turned twelve last month, and they had a party at the bowling alley. I haven't been bowling since I was a teenager... you have to wear those funny shoes they rent out, and I always worried about who wore them before me.
Have you ever had a period of time, even if just for a day, where you didn't think about your friend's death or feel guilty about it?

No, doctor, I... I thought I just said that. I feel like a broken record, but no. There isn't a single day. I keep telling them, I'm the reason she died. Because I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. It never leaves me, not for a minute. And now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. 

The church is just so cold lately, too. The drafts come right through those big wooden doors at the front. They're original to the building, you know, from 1922. Solid oak. My husband, God rest his soul, used to say oak was the only wood worth building furniture out of. He built this beautiful hope chest for our daughter when she got married. Lined the whole inside with cedar so the moths wouldn't get to the blankets. Moths are such a nuisance, aren't they? They got into my winter coats last year, ruined a perfectly good wool peacoat I bought at Macy's. Macy's always has the best sales right after Christmas. I used to take the bus downtown on December 26th just to look at the clearance racks. The bus fare was only a quarter back then. You dropped it right into that little glass box next to the driver. The driver on my route was a nice man named Frank, he always wore a crisp uniform with a little hat. Uniforms used to look so smart. Now at the grocery store, they just give us these flimsy green polo shirts to wear. They snag on everything, especially the sharp edges of the candy racks right by the register. I snagged mine twice last week ringing up peppermint patties. Peppermint is good for an upset stomach, my mother always said...
Do you think it's possible that your feelings of guilt are not based in reality?

Doctor, are we going in circles? I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall today. It is reality. I keep telling them, I am the reason my friend died. It's my fault because I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts about her sometimes. It is as real as you sitting there. And I know the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me. 

Pastor Thomas has been sweating so much during his sermons lately, just wiped out, you can see it right through his robes. He uses one of those little clip-on microphones now, so he can walk around the altar. Not the big heavy microphone on the wooden stand like Reverend Miller used to use. Reverend Miller had such a booming voice, he hardly needed a microphone anyway. But those little clip-on ones, they run on batteries. Just the regular double-A kind. We sell them right at the front of my register at the grocery store, right next to the gossip magazines. I really don't know who buys those magazines, they cost nearly five dollars now and it's all just nonsense about movie stars getting divorced. My husband and I were married for forty-two years. We went to Niagara Falls for our honeymoon... we took the train up. It was so loud, the water crashing down like that. We bought a little glass snow globe in the gift shop, but it broke when we moved into our house. Glass went absolutely everywhere. It is just impossible to get tiny pieces of glass out of a shag carpet, you know. You have to use a piece of soft bread to press into the carpet fibers to pick up the little shards. My mother taught me that trick with the bread. She always baked her own bread, white bread with a nice thick crust...
Have you ever had a time since your friend's death when you felt completely free of guilt?

Doctor, I just... I don't know how else to say it. Are you having trouble hearing me today? Because I keep telling them, and I'm telling you, I am the reason my friend died. I didn't call her back, and I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. There is no time I feel free of it, because it's the truth. And I know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me. 

I really think you might need to get your ears checked if you didn't hear me the first three times. My brother Arthur just got his hearing checked over at the VA hospital last month. They gave him those tiny little hearing aids that go right inside the ear canal, you can hardly even see them. They aren't anything like the big clunky beige ones our grandfather used to wear behind his ears. Grandpa used to just turn his off whenever Grandma started nagging him about smoking his pipe in the parlor. He smoked cherry tobacco, it came in a little tin pouch with a picture of an orchard on it. I always liked the smell of it, actually. It smelled sweet, kind of like the holidays. We used to string popcorn and cranberries for the Christmas tree when I was little. You have to use a very sharp needle to do that, or the popcorn just shatters into pieces. And you have to use day-old popcorn, too, so it's a little stale. If it's too fresh, it just crumbles in your hands. We'd pop it right on the stove in a heavy-bottomed pan with a little oil. You have to shake the pan back and forth the whole time so the kernels don't burn on the bottom. My wrist always got so tired shaking that heavy metal pan. I have quite a bit of arthritis in my right wrist now, mostly from ringing up groceries all these years. Scanning those heavy plastic gallons of milk really takes a toll on your joints...
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you didn't feel guilty about your friend's death?

Doctor, are you playing a trick on me? Is this some kind of memory test? Because I swear to you, I've answered this exact same question three times already. I don't know why you keep asking me the same thing over and over. I told you, I'm the reason she died. I didn't call her back when I should have, and I had those terrible, ugly thoughts about her. There is no moment where I don't feel it. And the Lord knows it too, that's why He's punishing everyone at the church. It's all because of me. 

I just don't understand why you keep asking. It reminds me of when my daughter was little, she used to ask "why" after every single thing I said. "Eat your peas, Susan." "Why?" "Because they're good for you." "Why?" It was enough to drive a person up the wall. We used to grow our own peas in a little garden out back when we lived on Elm Street. Sugar snap peas, they were so sweet you could eat them right off the vine. My husband built a beautiful trellis for them to climb up, out of some old lattice we had left over from fixing the porch. He was always so handy like that. He could fix just about anything with a roll of duct tape and some WD-40. WD-40 is a miracle worker, you know. I use it on the wheels of my shopping cart at work when they start to squeak. There's nothing worse than a squeaky shopping cart wheel, especially when you're trying to concentrate on scanning items. The barcode scanner at my register has been acting up lately, too. You have to run the items across it three or four times before it finally beeps. It really slows down the line, and people get so impatient these days. Everyone is always in such a rush to get somewhere. Where are they all going in such a hurry, anyway?
Do you believe your thoughts or feelings of guilt are exaggerated or unrealistic?

Exaggerated? Lord have mercy, doctor, are you even listening to a single word I say? I feel like I'm a broken record today. It is not exaggerated. I keep telling everyone, and I'll tell you again, I am the reason my friend passed away. I didn't call her back when I was supposed to, and I had those awful, ugly thoughts about her sometimes. It's just the plain truth. And I know the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me, it's as clear as day. 

The church roof even started leaking right over the choir loft last Sunday. The water was just dripping right down onto Mrs. Gable's sheet music. She plays the organ, you know. It's a beautiful old pipe organ, they had to have it shipped all the way from Boston back in the fifties, or maybe it was the early sixties. The brass pipes go all the way up to the ceiling, they're just massive. They have to hire a special tuner to come out from the city once a year to keep it sounding right. He's a very quiet man, always wears a little maroon bowtie. My husband used to wear a bowtie when we went out dancing, back when my knees still worked right. We used to go to the Elks Lodge on Saturday nights. They had a live band that played all the big band tunes. Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman... people actually knew how to dance together back then, not just jumping up and down like teenagers do now. I see them buying those energy drinks at my register, those big tall cans with the bright green monster claws on them. I don't know how their hearts don't just explode from all that caffeine and sugar. I can't even drink a cup of regular coffee after two o'clock in the afternoon or I'll be staring at the ceiling all night long. My mother was the same way, she only drank decaf Sanka...
Have you ever had a period of more than a week where you didn't think about your friend's death?

Doctor, are you deliberately trying to upset me? I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall. A week? No! I just... I don't understand why you keep asking me variations of the same thing. I've told you, I am the reason she died. I didn't return her call, and I had those ugly, wicked thoughts. It's constantly on my mind because it's the truth, and the Lord is punishing the whole congregation at church because of what I did. 

It's just like how it rained for forty days and forty nights, you know? Water is a powerful thing. It can wash away a whole town if the river gets high enough. We had a terrible flood back in '93, the water came right up to the front steps of the post office downtown. The mail carriers had to use little aluminum rowboats to get the mail out to the folks out on County Road 9. I remember seeing Mr. Henderson rowing his boat right down Main Street, wearing his little blue uniform shorts. He always wore shorts, even in November. He said it was because he walked so much his legs never got cold, but I think he just liked showing off his calves. He used to be a track star in high school, ran the 400-meter dash. My grandson runs track now, but he does the hurdles. I don't know how they jump over those things without tripping and breaking their necks. I tripped over a loose floor mat at the grocery store last Tuesday and nearly took out a whole endcap of canned baked beans. Bush's baked beans, the ones with the brown sugar and bacon. They're usually on sale two for three dollars this time of year, getting ready for all the summer barbecues. People buy so many hot dogs and buns, but they always forget the mustard. I must sell twenty bottles of yellow mustard on a Friday afternoon before a holiday weekend...
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt completely free of guilt about your friend's death?

Doctor, please. Are you trying to make me lose my mind? Why are you asking me the exact same thing again? Free of guilt? No. No, never. I keep telling you, I keep telling everyone, I am the reason she died. I didn't call her back when she needed me, and I had those terrible, ugly thoughts. How could I ever be free of that? The Lord knows what I did, and that's why He is punishing everybody at the church. It's my fault they're suffering. 

It's just like when you drop a stone in a pond, the ripples just keep going and going. We used to have a little koi pond in the backyard of the house on Elm Street. My husband dug it out himself with a shovel, took him three whole weekends. He put this thick black plastic liner in it and surrounded it with these beautiful flat river rocks he brought back from a fishing trip up in the mountains. We had three koi fish in there. One was bright orange, one was white with little red spots, and one was mostly black. They used to come right up to the surface when I'd sprinkle their food in. It smelled awful, that fish food, like dried up shrimp and seaweed. Reminds me of the smell near the seafood counter at work. They bleach the floors behind the counter every night, but you can still smell the fish in the morning when you open up the store. I usually work the early shift, clocking in at 6:00 AM. It's so quiet in the store then, before the music starts playing over the loudspeakers. They play the same loop of songs every single day. I swear, if I hear that one song by the Beach Boys one more time, I'm going to take a broom handle to the speaker above my register. "Kokomo," that's the one. It gets stuck in your head for hours. Aruba, Jamaica... I've never been to any of those places. The furthest I've ever traveled was to Florida to see my sister in 1988. She lived in a little condo down in Boca Raton...

I just don't understand why you keep asking. It reminds me of when my daughter was little, she used to ask "why" after every single thing I said. "Eat your peas, Susan." "Why?" "Because they're good for you." "Why?" It was enough to drive a person up the wall. We used to grow our own peas in a little garden out back when we lived on Elm Street. Sugar snap peas, they were so sweet you could eat them right off the vine. My husband built a beautiful trellis for them to climb up, out of some old lattice we had left over from fixing the porch. He was always so handy like that. He could fix just about anything with a roll of duct tape and some WD-40. WD-40 is a miracle worker, you know. I use it on the wheels of my shopping cart at work when they start to squeak. There's nothing worse than a squeaky shopping cart wheel, especially when you're trying to concentrate on scanning items. The barcode scanner at my register has been acting up lately, too. You have to run the items across it three or four times before it finally beeps. It really slows down the line, and people get so impatient these days. Everyone is always in such a rush to get somewhere. Where are they all going in such a hurry, anyway?

patient.answer:
Exaggerated? Lord have mercy, doctor, are you even listening to a single word I say? I feel like I'm a broken record today. It is not exaggerated. I keep telling everyone, and I'll tell you again, I am the reason my friend passed away. I didn't call her back when I was supposed to, and I had those awful, ugly thoughts about her sometimes. It's just the plain truth. And I know the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me, it's as clear as day. 

The church roof even started leaking right over the choir loft last Sunday. The water was just dripping right down onto Mrs. Gable's sheet music. She plays the organ, you know. It's a beautiful old pipe organ, they had to have it shipped all the way from Boston back in the fifties, or maybe it was the early sixties. The brass pipes go all the way up to the ceiling, they're just massive. They have to hire a special tuner to come out from the city once a year to keep it sounding right. He's a very quiet man, always wears a little maroon bowtie. My husband used to wear a bowtie when we went out dancing, back when my knees still worked right. We used to go to the Elks Lodge on Saturday nights. They had a live band that played all the big band tunes. Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman... people actually knew how to dance together back then, not just jumping up and down like teenagers do now. I see them buying those energy drinks at my register, those big tall cans with the bright green monster claws on them. I don't know how their hearts don't just explode from all that caffeine and sugar. I can't even drink a cup of regular coffee after two o'clock in the afternoon or I'll be staring at the ceiling all night long. My mother was the same way, she only drank decaf Sanka...

Doctor, are you deliberately trying to upset me? I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall. A week? No! I just... I don't understand why you keep asking me variations of the same thing. I've told you, I am the reason she died. I didn't return her call, and I had those ugly, wicked thoughts. It's constantly on my mind because it's the truth, and the Lord is punishing the whole congregation at church because of what I did. 

It's just like how it rained for forty days and forty nights, you know? Water is a powerful thing. It can wash away a whole town if the river gets high enough. We had a terrible flood back in '93, the water came right up to the front steps of the post office downtown. The mail carriers had to use little aluminum rowboats to get the mail out to the folks out on County Road 9. I remember seeing Mr. Henderson rowing his boat right down Main Street, wearing his little blue uniform shorts. He always wore shorts, even in November. He said it was because he walked so much his legs never got cold, but I think he just liked showing off his calves. He used to be a track star in high school, ran the 400-meter dash. My grandson runs track now, but he does the hurdles. I don't know how they jump over those things without tripping and breaking their necks. I tripped over a loose floor mat at the grocery store last Tuesday and nearly took out a whole endcap of canned baked beans. Bush's baked beans, the ones with the brown sugar and bacon. They're usually on sale two for three dollars this time of year, getting ready for all the summer barbecues. People buy so many hot dogs and buns, but they always forget the mustard. I must sell twenty bottles of yellow mustard on a Friday afternoon before a holiday weekend...

patient.answer:
Doctor, please. Are you trying to make me lose my mind? Why are you asking me the exact same thing again? Free of guilt? No. No, never. I keep telling you, I keep telling everyone, I am the reason she died. I didn't call her back when she needed me, and I had those terrible, ugly thoughts. How could I ever be free of that? The Lord knows what I did, and that's why He is punishing everybody at the church. It's my fault they're suffering. 

It's just like when you drop a stone in a pond, the ripples just keep going and going. We used to have a little koi pond in the backyard of the house on Elm Street. My husband dug it out himself with a shovel, took him three whole weekends. He put this thick black plastic liner in it and surrounded it with these beautiful flat river rocks he brought back from a fishing trip up in the mountains. We had three koi fish in there. One was bright orange, one was white with little red spots, and one was mostly black. They used to come right up to the surface when I'd sprinkle their food in. It smelled awful, that fish food, like dried up shrimp and seaweed. Reminds me of the smell near the seafood counter at work. They bleach the floors behind the counter every night, but you can still smell the fish in the morning when you open up the store. I usually work the early shift, clocking in at 6:00 AM. It's so quiet in the store then, before the music starts playing over the loudspeakers. They play the same loop of songs every single day. I swear, if I hear that one song by the Beach Boys one more time, I'm going to take a broom handle to the speaker above my register. "Kokomo," that's the one. It gets stuck in your head for hours. Aruba, Jamaica... I've never been to any of those places. The furthest I've ever traveled was to Florida to see my sister in 1988. She lived in a little condo down in Boca Raton...
